headline: Co4E is a visual workflow builder that lets users lay out multi-step AI agent workflows and run them; of the 14 tickets in this area, 7 are backed up by code we read and 7 could not be confirmed from the parts of the codebase examined.
what_is_there: The code shows a working node-graph workflow studio: a drag-and-drop canvas with zoom and pan, an execution engine that runs steps in dependency order and passes each step's output into the next, fan-out to multiple sub-agents with a join stage, custom agent personas, automatic self-verification rounds with a configurable limit, and run history with progress tracking and restore-on-startup.
what_is_unclear: The analysis could not confirm the finer workflow features — the full set of node types (Start, End, Join, IF/Switch), conditional branching and the skipping of gated branches, the Auto/Plan/Manual run modes, permission presets, workflow import/export between instances, and the newer attachment-folder and URL inputs on a step — mainly because the central workflow definition module and step editor were not among the files reviewed. Some searches also surfaced an unrelated model-routing 'switch' feature, which added noise rather than evidence.
suggested_action: Ask the team to walk through the core workflow definition module and the step editor screen, which between them should settle most of the seven open items in one pass.
